code.note: Fortran 95 code under F95/. The example driver is F95/Drivers/simple_example.f90 (program ODRPACK95_EXAMPLE, four data points, one response, two parameters with bounds). The shipped reference output is F95/Drivers/simple_example.out, the output of that driver. The ODRPACK95 source is in the archive's F95 source directory; the rerun has to build it with the driver.

claim.location: Shipped reference output F95/Drivers/simple_example.out, section 'Estimated BETA(J)', row J = 1. Claim value: BETA(1) = 1.63337057 at the end of the fit (INFO = 1, sum-of-squares convergence, NITER = 25).

reference.sha256: not computed; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: First estimated parameter BETA(1) of the explicit ODR fit in simple_example.f90, as printed by ODRPACK95 (E format, 9 significant digits).
claim.paper_value: The paper's own examples are not read. The value is the shipped simple_example.out.

tolerance.basis: The reference prints 9 significant digits, so rounding is about 5e-9. The fit stops at PARTOL = 3.67e-11 and SSTOL = 1.49e-8, so a correct build of the same code should agree to well below 1e-6 absolute, while a wrong derivative or a broken bound would move BETA(1) by far more. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

why: The shipped example is a small bounded ODR fit whose printed estimate is not a closed form; a rerun must run the Fortran 95 ODR iteration, including its derivative and stopping rules, to reproduce BETA(1).
